dakar-ter-phase1.why: Seneweb page opens and carries every quoted fact: the AfDB froze over 9 billion CFA francs of the second tranche, set a 11 November deadline for the outstanding social debt, reminded Senegal of its obligation to correct the identified shortcomings, and AFD suspended funding six times. But all of it is dated to the 2026 second-phase financing review, years after the displacement began in 2016. The page also says nothing about any condition attached to the original financing. Post-harm terms are not conditions, so the only sentence the ct rested on is stripped and nothing is left.

phnom-penh-sugar-kampong-speu.why: Page opens. It confirms the 2010 assessment recommended a detailed impact assessment under the Equator Principles and IFC Performance Standards, that ANZ 'proceeded with a corporate loan to Phnom Penh Sugar without ensuring that such assessment would be conducted', the February 2020 commitment of the gross profit on the loan, and 1,096 families. But the page nowhere states that no condition was attached to the loan: it simply never mentions loan covenants. 'none' therefore fails the rule that a source must say so, and is removed. What remains is a recommendation (not a condition) and a 2020 settlement (after the harm), so nothing qualifies.

wwf-cameroon-baka-ecoguards.why: Report opens. All four quoted facts check out: 'WWF does not have a role in appointing or directing ecoguards'; it 'continued to fund, support and collaborate with ecoguards in a variety of ways'; 'None of the agreements and MOUs established in the period covered by this report' contain human rights provisions for state agencies; and the panel recommends WWF make clear that adopting an ecoguard code of conduct and related measures 'are requirements for WWF continuing to provide support to the ecoguards'. But the panel's finding is that the agreements lack human rights provisions, which is narrower than a statement that no condition was attached to the money. 'none' is an inference, not a source statement, so it is removed, and the text names no requirement.

amibara-afar-grazing-lands.why: Audit opens. It quotes the Staff Appraisal Report at para 4.20: 'assurances were obtained that should groundwater levels rise so as to affect the productivity of soils in the Project area' and 'Government would make available to AVDA the funds needed to meet the cost of installing additional water-table control facilities'. Para 1.5 gives the settlement of 'some 800 Afar families (about 4,000 people) on 2,000 ha' as a project component. Para 4.13: 'the Afars have neither been compensated nor have they been involved in the development effort'. The audit names no other covenant. safeguard rests on an environmental undertaking obtained with the credit, so it stands.

gujarat-medium-irrigation-oustees.why: Completion report opens. Para 5.20: 'The SAR and legal documents required that GOG: (i) prepare an integrated overall plan for rehabilitation', plus the nine priority sub-project plans, a rehabilitation committee in each sub-project and rehabilitation under the Schedule A guidelines. Section 9.4 gives the water charge covenant as 'establishment of water charges to recover the full O&M cost and a reasonable portion of the capital cost', not complied with; section 7.2 gives the 31 March review and 'No revision had taken place since 1984'. Section 5.4 cites 'conditionalities for extending the credit further'. safeguard and fees both supported.

ramagundam-ntpc-oustees.why: Section 3.01 confirms the credit and loan 'were made effective on May 4, 1979' 'following execution of the subsidiary loan agreement between GOI and NTPC'. Section 5.01 confirms NTPC was to sell power to the SEBs 'under bulk supply contracts satisfactory to the Bank' and that GOI was to ensure undertakings to purchase at least 85% of output. The land and resettlement figures (4,116 hectares, 2,279 families affected, 782 resettled) are in section 3.07 with no covenant attached. Two corrections: (1) section 5.03 presents the 9.5% rate of return as what 'the appraisal report forecast', not as a requirement, so that sentence is removed; (2) the ct 'prices' is removed - its quote mentions a return on fixed assets, not any price or tariff, and the report ties no tariff covenant to this loan. The 85% offtake undertaking is a real requirement but no type on the list covers an offtake undertaking; 'repay' was not added because adding types is outside a check.

farakka-ntpc-oustees.why: Part I para 9 confirms the effectiveness conditions (bulk power sale contracts plus a subsidiary loan agreement 'satisfactory to the Bank'), four extensions, and 'The loan finally became effective on August 30, 1985'. Part I para 41: 'the resettlement and rehabilitation (R&R) aspects of the project were not formally addressed' at appraisal, and the guidelines 'were agreed between the Bank and NTPC in 1993' under Loan 3632-IN. Two corrections: the rate-of-return covenant is stated in fiscal years ('7 percent through FY90 and 9.5 percent during FY91 through FY95'), not calendar years, so the dates are fixed; and ct 'prices' is removed because the quote names a return on assets, not a price or tariff.

ruzizi-ii-indemnities.why: Report opens. Para 5.06: effectiveness depended on 'proof that the land and rights were under the ownership and control of SINELAC', and SINELAC was to 'take all necessary steps to acquire land and rights in respect of land'; the Bank deemed 'the impact of the project on the local population' 'inconsequential' and required no resettlement plan. Para 5.16: the average sales price was to be set to achieve 'a 10% rate of return over the life of the project'. Para 5.18: failing to price power as agreed 'would prevent extension of the Closing Date of the three IDA credits'. land and prices both supported; prices here is tied to a sales price, not to a return on assets.

gorgol-foum-gleita.why: Report opens. Para 22 lists the effectiveness conditions as described, including proof that the IFAD, Islamic Development Bank, Saudi Fund and Libya agreements were effective and the other co-financier agreements signed. Paras 72-73: at negotiations SONADER agreed to collect water charges of 'UM12,000/ha/year' and none were collected in the first full cultivation year. Para 26 confirms 'a protocol was drawn up between the Government and traditional land owners'. The report describes no displacement or compensation terms. fees is supported by a cost-recovery charge agreed at loan negotiations.

kiambere-dam-resettlement.why: Audit opens. Para 2.6 confirms the two effectiveness conditions. Paras 2.21-2.22 confirm the lease fee of debt service plus a 'development surcharge' equal to 15% of total cost, with the offtaker bearing 'all operating costs including repairs and replacement'. Paras 2.20-2.21 confirm the covenant to 'earn 8 percent on average net revalued fixed assets of the entire power sector', 'lowered retroactively to 6 percent from 8 percent for 1985'. Para 2.13 confirms the major share of works was reserved for companies from the financing countries. Para 2.25 confirms 'neither the project description nor the loan covenants anticipated it'. Two corrections: (1) the environmental impact study and panel of experts sentence is removed - the audit shows these as bank-wide policy, not loan terms: para 2.24 has the Bank saying the study 'was a requirement in a project of this magnitude' after noting it had not been done, and para 2.12 quotes a Bank letter that 'the Bank now requires a Panel of Experts to be appointed for large hydro projects'; general policy does not count, so 'safeguard' goes with it. (2) 'prices' is removed: the quote names a return on revalued fixed assets, not a price, and the audit sets out no tariff formula in the covenant. tied and repay stand.

nangbeto-dam-resettlement.why: Study opens. Section 10.2 confirms the side letter to the Development Credit Agreement under which the government and CEB undertook to continue 'detailed work on resettlement...for at least three years after reservoir filling', that 'there is no evidence that anything was done' and that the side letter was 'totally ignored'. Section 10.1: 'The Bank stipulated that an adequate plan be prepared in time'. Section 2.3 confirms the deadline came from the Staff Appraisal Report ('a more detailed plan would be provided by December 31, 1985'), and section 2.4 that CEB met it. safeguard rests on an undertaking in a side letter to the credit agreement, so it stands.

indonesia-regional-cities-transport.why: Report opens and every sentence checks out: para 51 'cities were requested to appoint selected key staff as a condition of loan effectiveness'; para 54 the loan-agreement action plan and the five-year investment plan updates, both partly complied with; para 50 land acquisition and resettlement discussed in the SAR and confirmed during negotiations; para 42 no special resettlement plan, no baseline surveys, and families without title receiving significantly less than those with full title. The ct 'law' is removed: the quote is about an urban transport planning action plan, which is not a change to law, and no type on the list covers a planning or staffing requirement. The conditions text is left as verified.

opened: https://documents1.worldbank.org/curated/en/604031510069124056/text/multi-page.txt (read twice, including a targeted pass on every sentence containing 'royalt')
uganda-forestry-kibale-evictions.why: Audit opens. Confirmed: the Development Credit Agreement held only a conventional provision on government funding of operations, which the audit judges inadequate; 'the project should have required an appropriate resettlement plan: it did not'; the August 1986 telex that the Bank 'must assume nobody will be evicted as a result of our project'; 'Bank policy makes resettlement planning mandatory'; and 'The study of encroachment included in the project was never carried out'. The royalty claim does not hold. The audit never calls the royalty rates a covenant or a condition. Section 3.11 says only 'In agreement with IDA, royalty rates for timber were increased and collection was improved' - a description of what happened, not a term the money depended on. The two-year cycle comes from footnote 14, 'The change cycle is biennial rather than annual, as was agreed with IDA', which is ambiguous and may mean the opposite of what the entry says. That sentence is removed and ct 'prices' with it; a royalty is in any case a charge on timber, not a price condition.

jabotabek-urban-compensation.why: Covenant table (ICR Table 10, Loan 2932-IND) opens and confirms all four covenants: Schedule 5 para 6 required land acquisition and resettlement under 'a plan and implementation schedule satisfactory to the Bank', status not complied with, 'Plan not prepared or agreed'; para 7 local tax revenues up 'at least 6% per year in real terms'; para 8 property tax (PBB) revenues up 'at least 13% per year in real terms' jointly with DGPajak; para 9 development grants and urban infrastructure allocations not to exceed 'FY88/89 levels in nominal terms'. The note that later projects made resettlement planning 'a condition of disbursement' while this loan's covenant was not tied to disbursement also checks out. One correction: the budget covenant is a ceiling ('not to exceed'), not a requirement to hold allocations at that level, so the wording and the 'cuts' quote are fixed. safeguard, tax and cuts stand.

kulekhani-hydro-resettlement.why: Audit opens. The Evaluation Summary names 'the condition of effectiveness on tariff increases'. Para 3.18 gives the four covenants in the order the entry gives them, including 'tariffs would be increased to enable NEC to earn a rate of return' and 'a resettlement plan for persons affected by the Project would be finalized in consultation with IDA'. Para 3.15: 'The Government agreed at negotiations to discontinue this tax', a royalty tax of about US 0.08 cents/kWh. Para 7.03: 'the Borrower failed to implement tariff increases according to the schedule included in the Appraisal Report', and para 4.30 that the rate of return covenant was not satisfied. prices here is tied to an explicit tariff increase, so it stands, as do safeguard and tax.

antananarivo-plain-enterprises.why: Audit opens. The memorandum confirms the credit agreement's own timeline for the flood control agency ('to be established not until almost three years after Board presentation') and that the agency came about five years after Board approval, with para 22 putting the two institutions 'some four years into the project'. Para 12 confirms the delays from 'problems with the acquisition of land necessary for the drainage works' and 'the resettlement of people affected by the project', and the document does not say a resettlement plan was required. The ct 'law' is removed: creating a management agency is an institutional step, and the quote names no change to law.

opened: https://documents1.worldbank.org/curated/en/145171640308880262/text/Sierra-Leone-Freetown-Emergency-Recovery-Project.txt (read twice, including a targeted pass on every mention of RAP, RRAP, ARAP and the Safeguards Action Plan)
freetown-red-zone-demolitions.why: Para 64 confirms 'the Safeguards Action Plan was included in the PAD to ensure implementation readiness', sequencing the required safeguard instruments. Para 66 confirms the contractors' project-wide gender-based violence and violence-against-children action plan within their environmental and social management plans, the Bank's determination that OP 4.12 applied, the government's social audit and the plan 'approved by the Bank in April 2019', and the audit findings on tenants, caretakers and underpaid homeowners. One correction: the plan covering the landslide site was a Retroactive Resettlement Action Plan prepared after the government's own evacuation and demolitions, not a Resettlement Action Plan required in advance, and the Abbreviated Resettlement Action Plan covers components 1.2 and 1.3 (with payments also under 2.2), not 'the other two components'. The sentence and the 'why' quote are rewritten to the pre-existing requirement in the appraisal document, which does carry safeguard.

xayaburi-dam-thai-banks.why: Profile opens (last updated 2016-10-12). It confirms Kasikornbank 'awaiting a clearer EIA report for the project' and its 'strict social and environmental guidelines for financial support', that the assessment 'was only released to the public in mid-March 2011' after the consultations, and that it 'only considered a ten kilometre radius below the dam site'. But the Siam Commercial Bank line is printed as 'If it doesn't comply with the law, we would not sign the loan agreemen' and was reworded in the entry; more importantly it is a bank officer's statement of intent before signing, not a published loan term, and BankTrack quotes no loan agreement and ties no resettlement requirement to the loans. A bank statement does not show the money depended on anything, so safeguard and the text go.

theun-hinboun-expansion.why: Profile opens (last updated 2015-11-01). Confirmed: 'This project has been identified as an Equator Project'; the 2009 findings 'indicate that the Theun Hinboun Expansion Project is not in compliance with the Equator Principles and Lao national law'; and 'Despite promises in the Concession Agreement to set up a panel of experts'. But the ct quote is only that BankTrack lists the project as an Equator Principles project. Equator Principles applicability is a bank-wide framework, not a published term of these loans, and the profile names no lender requirement on resettlement or compensation. The panel of experts comes from the concession agreement, not the loans. Nothing shows the money depended on anything, so the entry is blanked.

rapu-rapu-cyanide-spills-2005.why: Profile opens (last updated 2015-11-01) and confirms 'The lender group that was involved in the mine until April 2008 had declared the Equator Principles applicable' and 'ABN AMRO sector policy on mining should also have been applied to this operation'. The page carries no loan agreement, no covenant and no security term, and BankTrack gives no source for the Equator Principles line. A declaration that a standard applies, plus a statement that a bank's own sector policy 'should also have been applied', is general policy, not a term the money depended on, so safeguard and the text go. The Greenpeace-commissioned 'Fool's Gold' report was not opened; the surety bond it describes is a Pollution Adjudication Board requirement, not a lender one, so it would not have counted either way.

santo-antonio-dam-madeira.why: Both pages open. BankTrack confirms 'This project has been identified as an Equator Project' and names no condition on Santander's lending. Renewable Energy World confirms BNDES 'approved 6.1 billion reais (US$2.5 billion) in financing', 'funded 46.6 percent of the project amount', 'was granted to Santo Antonio Energia (SAESA)', 'set requirements that will enable utility companies to provide affordable rates to consumers', and 'social investments of 50 million reais (US$20.9 million), as suggested by BNDES'. Two problems. The clause saying Santander passed BNDES funds on to the project company is not on either page I opened, so it is removed. And ct 'prices' is removed: the article does not say what the requirements were, does not say the money depended on them, and BNDES is not one of this case's named lenders, so the finding is about a different lender's money. The verified figures are kept as text.

smb-boke-bauxite.why: Report opens. Confirmed: the IFC's 2006 loan to ICICI was to 'address the funding needs of a top performing bank' with no conditions named; ICICI's share of the China Hongqiao loan was 'to be used for general corporate purposes'; and IFC financial-sector clients 'are required to implement the institution's social and environmental Performance Standards'. The report does not mention SMB or Winning International at all. The ct rests entirely on that last line, which is a general statement about all IFC financial-sector clients, not a term of the ICICI loan, so safeguard goes. Nor does the report say no condition was attached, so 'none' would not have been available either.

kaltim-prima-coal-dayak-basap.why: Report opens and every sentence checks out: the January 2014 equity investment 'was done with the condition that it be down-streamed' to the subsidiaries in Russia, Bosnia, Kosovo and Poland and 'was recorded as a capital increase in each of these subsidiaries'; the IFC's unevidenced claim that the Axis Bank bond proceeds were limited to projects in India, against an offering circular saying proceeds 'shall be used for enhancing long term resources for funding infrastructure and affordable housing'; and that the 2016 Coal Policy came 'based on IFC's recommendation', which the entry correctly does not call a condition. The ct 'tied' is removed: on this list 'tied' means tied procurement, using the lender country's contractor, and this is a restriction on where the money could go, which no type covers. The text is left as verified.
